prompt.context_jp: 「普通のドクターなら止血することだけを優先して考えたと思います。でも…甘春先生___違いました」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「甘春先生___違いました」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits best here?

feedback.correct_en: Igarashi is contrasting Dr. Amakasu with the 'ordinary doctor' he just described. は marks that contrastive topic: 'other doctors would have…, but YOU were different.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce Amakasu as new information, losing the explicit contrast with 普通のドクター that drives the whole line.

contrast_examples.jp: 他の人はやめた。でも彼は続けた。
contrast_examples.en: Others quit. But he kept going. (contrastive は)

contrast_examples.jp: 誰か来た。山田さんが来た。
contrast_examples.en: Someone came. It was Yamada. (identificational が)

prompt.context_jp: 空港で五十嵐に向かって叫ぶ若き日の甘春。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あなた___手出しできないくらい優秀な放射線科医になってみせます」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle does young Amakasu use here?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative clause ('a radiologist that YOU can't interfere with'), the subject of the embedded clause typically takes が. It also carries exhaustive focus — specifically you, Igarashi.
feedback.incorrect_en: は rarely appears as the subject of a relative clause; it would also drop the pointed, exhaustive 'even you' feeling she's expressing.

contrast_examples.en: the dish he made (subject in relative clause → が)
He made the dish. (main-clause topic は)

prompt.context_jp: 再会の場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 目の前に立つ甘春___、二年前より少しだけ、その眼差しに重みを増していた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence makes a comment ABOUT Amakasu (she has gained a gravity in her gaze). That topic-comment structure calls for は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn this into new-information reporting, but she's already the center of the scene — not someone being newly introduced.

contrast_examples.en: She has changed. (comment on known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 甘春の独白の続き。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「患者と向き合うことでしか救えない命___ある」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The existential pattern 〜がある introduces 'there are lives that…' as new information — exactly what が is for.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose those lives as an already-known topic, but she's asserting their existence for the first time.

contrast_examples.en: There are such people. (existence, new info)
As for such people, there are none. (contrast/topic)

prompt.context_jp: 灰島が甘春の処置に不満を述べる場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「今回たまたまうまくいったからよかったものの、あなたの取った行動___訴訟に発展してた恐れだってあるんですよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle is used here?

feedback.correct_en: Haijima is contrasting the lucky outcome with the risky action: 'things worked out, BUT your action (by contrast) could have led to a lawsuit.' Contrastive は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would flatly introduce her action as new, losing the 'but on the other hand' pivot the sentence builds around.

contrast_examples.jp: 結果は良かった。でも方法は危険だった。
contrast_examples.en: The result was good. But the method (in contrast) was dangerous.
The method was the problem. (identifying it)

prompt.context_jp: 看護師が読影室に飛び込んでくる。
prompt.prompt_jp: バイオリニストの宝生真凛___、検査を終えたにもかかわらず立ち上がれずにいるという。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this news-like report?

feedback.correct_en: Marin is being introduced as new information in the narrative — a specific person who (surprisingly) can't stand. が marks that newly introduced subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat Marin as an already-established topic, but the narrator is bringing her onto the scene for the first time.

prompt.context_jp: 位相方向を変えて撮り直した画像を見る場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 曖昧に霞んでいた延髄外側の一点___、はっきりとした信号として浮かび上がっていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this discovery moment?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence reports a new observation emerging on screen — が marks that newly discovered subject appearing in the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose the point as a known topic, but it's just now becoming visible as the finding.

contrast_examples.en: The shadow was already gone. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 五十嵐が診断を告げる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「真凛さんを苦しめてる病気___おそらくワレンベルグ症候群です」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle makes this diagnosis statement natural?

feedback.correct_en: 'The disease troubling Marin' is the topic; the comment identifies what it is. The classic 〜はＸです pattern uses は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively point to 'the disease' as the one unique item (odd here), whereas he's naming what the already-discussed illness is.

contrast_examples.jp: この病気はワレンベルグです。
ワレンベルグがこの病気です。

prompt.context_jp: 退院会見のお膳立ての場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 真の功労者の名を伏せたまま、灰島院長の手柄として発表する筋書き___、着々と組み立てられていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The 'scenario' is introduced here as new information — a plot being assembled behind the scenes. Descriptive が fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat the scenario as already established, but the narrator is revealing its existence to us now.

prompt.context_jp: 田中が実は新人扱いされている説明。
prompt.prompt_jp: 新参ではないはずの彼___、勤務歴だけで見ればなぜか一番の新入りに位置づけられているのだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence sets up a contrast: 'he (who shouldn't be a newcomer)… yet is ranked as one.' Contrastive/topic は fits this 'as for him' framing.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce him as new info, but he's already a known character being commented on with a surprising twist.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼はベテランなのに、新人扱いだ。
contrast_examples.en: He's a veteran, yet he's treated as a newbie. (contrastive は)

prompt.context_jp: 灰島が数字を無視できなくなる場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: だが今回に限っては、放射線科の働き___読影件数の増加という数字となって現れつつある。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The narration spotlights the radiology team's work as the new, specific thing that's now showing up as numbers — が introduces that subject into focus.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a generic topic comment, but 今回に限っては already sets the frame; what's new in the sentence is the work itself appearing in the data.

contrast_examples.jp: 努力が結果となって現れた。
contrast_examples.en: Their effort showed up as results. (new subject → が)
Effort doesn't betray you. (generic topic → は)

prompt.context_jp: にぎやかな控室の描写の締め。
prompt.prompt_jp: だが、その騒がしさこそ___、この部屋の日常であり、結束の証でもあった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits with こそ here?

feedback.correct_en: こそ+が emphasizes exclusivity: 'it is precisely THIS noisiness (and nothing else) that is their daily life.' Exhaustive が pairs naturally with こそ.
feedback.incorrect_en: は after こそ is possible in some set phrases but loses the pointed 'exactly this one' identification the sentence needs.

contrast_examples.en: This is precisely the real thing.

prompt.context_jp: 再会の場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 甘春杏___、白衣の裾を揺らしてそこに立っていたのである。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this reveal?

feedback.correct_en: The 〜のである reveal spotlights Amakasu as the figure he just noticed — classic new-information/identificational が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame her as the already-established topic, which deflates the reveal of 'it was An standing there.'

contrast_examples.jp: そこに立っていたのは彼女だった。
contrast_examples.en: The one standing there was her. (cleft reveal)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女はそこに立っていた。

prompt.context_jp: IVR室の冒頭。
prompt.prompt_jp: モニターの前を離れられずにいたの___、久しぶりに白衣を纏った五十嵐唯織だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the cleft structure?

feedback.correct_en: This is a cleft: '[The one who couldn't leave the monitor] was Igarashi.' The nominalized clause is the topic — は — while the 'who' is identified in the predicate.
feedback.incorrect_en: が here would be ungrammatical in this のは〜だった cleft pattern.

contrast_examples.en: The one who stayed was him.

prompt.context_jp: 甘春が感情を抑えきれない場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 胸の奥から込み上げてくるもの___、彼女は隠しきれずにいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: 隠す takes a direct object, and the fronted phrase 'what welled up' is that object — を marks it even when moved to the front.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would clash with 隠しきれず, which needs an object, not a subject, for 'hide.'

prompt.context_jp: 場面転換。
prompt.prompt_jp: 数日後、甘春は市内の産科病棟の一室___訪ねていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits with 訪ねる here?

feedback.correct_en: 訪ねる takes を to mark the place/person visited as its direct object: 'visit a room.'
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks a location where an action happens, but 訪ねる doesn't take で for the thing being visited.

contrast_examples.en: I worked at the hospital. (de = location of action)

prompt.context_jp: 甘春がようやく口にする一言。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あの約束___くれて」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the blank — she's thanking him for keeping the promise.

feedback.correct_en: 約束を守る is the fixed collocation for 'keep a promise.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 保つ means 'maintain (a state)' and doesn't pair with 約束; 続ける ('continue') doesn't fit a one-time promise either.

prompt.context_jp: 甘春が五十嵐の言葉に何も返せずに立っている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 甘春は返す言葉を___、しばらくの間ただ立ち尽くしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb best fits 'at a loss for words'?

feedback.correct_en: 探しあぐねる means 'search in vain / struggle to find' — exactly her state of searching for a reply she can't come up with.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見つけ出し ('found') contradicts 'stood speechless'; 言い出して ('started to say') doesn't match the following 立ち尽くす.

contrast_examples.en: Struggled in vain to find an answer.

prompt.context_jp: 灰島が甘春に退室を求める。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「その理想に当院の規律を乱されるわけにはいきません。お___ください」
prompt.prompt_en: Which polite phrase tells her to leave?

feedback.correct_en: お引き取りください is the stiff, polite-but-cold business expression for 'please leave,' matching Haijima's cold formality.
feedback.incorrect_en: お帰りください is too casual/warm for a dismissal; お退きください is unidiomatic in this context.

contrast_examples.jp: お気をつけてお帰りください。

prompt.context_jp: 甘春が産科病棟で菊島に声をかける。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the standard congratulation.

choices.text: おめでとうございます

feedback.correct_en: ご出産おめでとうございます is the fixed phrase for congratulating a birth.
feedback.incorrect_en: お疲れさま acknowledges effort; 失礼します is an excuse-me/leave-taking. Neither congratulates.

contrast_examples.jp: ご結婚おめでとうございます。

prompt.context_jp: アーチファクトの説明。
prompt.prompt_jp: アーチファクトとは、読み損ねれば目も当てられない___を招く厄介な存在だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes this clinical warning?

feedback.correct_en: 誤診 ('misdiagnosis') is the specific medical term; the whole sentence is about misreading imaging.
feedback.incorrect_en: 誤解 is 'misunderstanding' (interpersonal), 誤算 is 'miscalculation' (plans) — neither matches a clinical reading error.

prompt.context_jp: 二年ぶりの再会で甘春が五十嵐に言う一言。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___ 五十嵐さん」
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrase does she say to welcome him back?

feedback.correct_en: おかえりなさい welcomes someone back — exactly right for his return from America.
feedback.incorrect_en: いってらっしゃい sends someone off; はじめまして is for first meetings.

contrast_examples.jp: ただいま。— おかえり。
行ってきます。— いってらっしゃい。
contrast_examples.en: I'm off. — Have a good one.

prompt.context_jp: 院長室に入って話を切り出す甘春。
prompt.prompt_jp: 胸のうちで幾度も___きた言葉を、彼女は一気に押し出すように吐き出した。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits 'mulled over repeatedly'?

feedback.correct_en: 反芻する ('ruminate / chew over') pairs naturally with 胸のうちで and 幾度も for 'turning over in one's mind.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 反省 is 'self-reflect/regret'; 反対 is 'oppose.' Neither matches silently rehearsing words.

prompt.context_jp: 鏑木が灰島の皮肉をかわす。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私はただ副院長としての仕事を___までです」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the humble/matter-of-fact verb form.

feedback.correct_en: 〜したまでです ('I merely did X') is a set humble/deflective expression. した fits the register.
feedback.incorrect_en: やった is too casual for his composed副院長 voice; できた ('was able to') changes the meaning entirely.

contrast_examples.jp: 自分の仕事をしたまでです。

prompt.context_jp: 五十嵐が「普通のドクターなら…」と前置きした上で続ける一言。
prompt.prompt_en: Which continuation sounds more natural as a contrastive follow-up?

choices.text: でも…甘春先生は違いました
でも…甘春先生が違いました

feedback.correct_en: After setting up 'an ordinary doctor would…,' the contrast with Dr. Amakasu calls for contrastive は. This is how the scene actually plays.
feedback.incorrect_en: が here would sound like identificational 'it was Amakasu who was different,' which fits a 'who?' question — not the 'but she, in contrast' flow.

contrast_examples.jp: 他の人はダメだった。でも彼女は違った。
contrast_examples.en: Others failed. But she was different.
The one who was different was her. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 甘春が院長室で復職を懇願する場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural as a formal plea to the director?

choices.text: お願いします こちらで働かせてください
お願いします こちらで働きたいです

feedback.correct_en: The causative-request 働かせてください ('please let me work') is the standard humble formula for asking permission from a superior.
feedback.incorrect_en: 働きたいです just states a desire; it's too flat and doesn't actually ask for permission, which weakens the plea.

contrast_examples.jp: ここで働かせてください。

contrast_examples.en: I want to work here. (bare preference)

prompt.context_jp: 五十嵐が二年ぶりに控室に戻ってきて挨拶する。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural for rejoining the team?

choices.text: 今日からまたよろしくお願いします
今日からまたよろしくしてください

feedback.correct_en: よろしくお願いします is the standard set phrase for asking to be in someone's good graces going forward.
feedback.incorrect_en: よろしくしてください sounds like a literal, awkward translation; native speakers don't request 'good treatment' that way.

contrast_examples.jp: よろしくお願いします。
contrast_examples.en: I look forward to working with you.

contrast_examples.jp: 今後ともよろしくお願いいたします。
contrast_examples.en: I hope for your continued favor. (more formal)

prompt.context_jp: 甘春が赤ん坊の前で呟く独白。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural as her reflective complaint?

choices.text: 目に見える効率性ばかりが優先される世の中だけど
目に見える効率性ばかりは優先される世の中だけど

feedback.correct_en: ばかりが優先される is the natural collocation — ばかり already does the 'only/nothing but' work, and が carries the subject into the passive 'be prioritized.'
feedback.incorrect_en: ばかりは in this slot sounds off; は after ばかり generally needs a contrastive follow-up and feels unnatural with 優先される here.

contrast_examples.jp: お金ばかりが大事にされる。

contrast_examples.en: This one thing I can't give up. (ばかり/だけ+は for emphatic contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 五十嵐が甘春の手技を讃える一言。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural as his heartfelt praise?

choices.text: 僕なんか手出しできないくらい素晴らしい手技でした
僕なんて手出しできないくらい素晴らしい手技がありました

feedback.correct_en: 〜素晴らしい手技でした directly evaluates what he just watched. It mirrors her promise from years ago ('優秀な放射線科医になってみせます') and lands with emotional precision.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手技がありました ('there was a procedure') shifts to a distant existential report, flattening the compliment and breaking the callback to her past vow.

contrast_examples.en: That was a splendid procedure. (direct evaluation)

contrast_examples.jp: 見事な手技がありました。
contrast_examples.en: There was a splendid procedure. (detached, report-like)
